description:
## Goal

Repair the draft stack so every pull request, branch, commit, and closed ticket names the same atomic change before the runtime-intrinsic cutover is reworked. The old #148 misleadingly contains fz-5xp.30, fz-kdt.22, and fz-tfn.67 while its title/body describe only .30.

## Verified state and disposition

The live trunk is `origin/main` at `de95e24`. The frozen uncommitted fz-tfn.62 candidate remains outside this work and must remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

The old remote stack #130 was `main -> #128 -> #129 -> #131…#139 -> #147 -> #148`. Replay established this retained graph, each branch one rebased commit with focused validation: `main -> #128 -> #131 -> #132 -> #133 -> #134 -> #135 -> #136 -> #137 -> #147`.

Do not preserve these old layers:

- #129 is superseded by merged #146, #150, and #151; it is the removed named `fn`/`fnp` compatibility route.
- #138/fz-5xp.81 turns direct Enum choices into 24 helper identities and 62 clauses, raises causal work, weakens a less-work gate, adds unreachable repair clauses, and creates raw-source-text authority. Its useful measurements belong as hypotheses in existing fz-5xp.85, not as this implementation.
- #139/fz-5xp.93 adds unused Enum.slice surface to rescue dead protocol scaffolding, duplicates an erased callback shape with receiver-specific reconstruction and impossible-state repairs, overlaps fz-5xp.85, and preserves a known composed-stride bug. Its correct outcome is deletion of unused scaffold, owned by its reopened ticket.
- The old #148/.30 commit introduces rejected user-visible `intrinsic` syntax and multiple semantic authorities. It must not be mechanically conflict-resolved or repushed. Reopened fz-5xp.30 owns a fresh correct-by-construction implementation; fz-kdt.22 and fz-tfn.67 remain safety-held commits for a later truthful stack.

## Correct stack operation

After recording safety refs and exact parent/patch evidence, use `gh stack` to drop only #129, #138, #139, and #148 from the local/remote stack graph. Then force-with-lease push the retained branches in their direct-parent order and let `gh stack submit` update their PR bases and remote stack topology. Close the obsolete PRs and delete their remote branches only after `gh stack`, PR bases, merge bases, and descendant reachability prove that nothing depends on them.

No broad unstack, main rewrite, source implementation change, compatibility branch, or frozen-worktree mutation is allowed.

## Acceptance

- The retained graph above is visible both locally and in `gh stack`; every retained PR has exactly one truthful ticket commit and exact direct base.
- Each force update uses the observed old remote head as its `--force-with-lease` expectation, after its direct parent CI is green.
- #129, #138, #139, and old #148 are absent from the resulting stack, closed, and their branches deleted only after no open descendant refers to them.
- fz-5xp.81 and fz-5xp.93 descriptions record their rejection/deletion outcomes; no contradictory comments stand as authority.
- fz-5xp.30 remains blocked pending its new one-authority implementation; .22/.67 are neither lost nor smuggled into another PR.
- The frozen .62 fingerprint, clean worktrees, direct-parent merge bases, PR commit lists, range equivalence for retained layers, and CI state are recorded.

## Review

A fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review must check the retained graph, parent sequencing, exact leases, justifications for dropped layers, remote PR boundaries, closed/deleted branch safety, and the frozen .62 fingerprint before close.
title: Rebuild #148 as a truthful stack before the intrinsic cutover
